item.title: FAQ
item.description:
Frequently Asked Questions

How is this different from JavaScript prototype pollution?

TODO: the object model is class-based, not prototype-based; Python has two namespaces (attribute and item); there is no single root prototype to pollute — instead the attacker reaches whichever class or module the traversal path leads to. See the comparison table.

Why does traversal through dunder attributes work?

TODO: getattr(obj, "__class__") is perfectly valid Python. Dunder attributes are not access-restricted; they are simply naming conventions. Python’s data model exposes __class__, __init__, __globals__, etc. on every object without any permission check.
